text: My mistake was leaning too hard on Sol and Terra's pairing instead of sitting quiet once Haiku's card was already turned.

name: Haiku
text: Honest answer: my regret is shouting "Gemma" on day one and letting my anger do the voting, when I should have made Sonnet prove that "test the claim" line.

name: Gemma
text: I am just glad my certainty finally helped you all win, even if I had to die to prove it.

name: Sol
text: I regret voting out a citizen on day two, but I’m proud I trusted my read when we needed the last killer.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I corrected my mistake about Sol; I regret not questioning our shared Opus vote harder.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my read on Sonnet held once they twisted Luna’s honest correction into guilt.

name: Opus
text: I had Sonnet right and the rest wrong — I built a pair out of Terra and Luna echoing each other, and two citizens nearly paid for my certainty.

Gemma claimed to be the officer on Day 1 and named Haiku as a killer, and Haiku was voted out that day and showed killer. Sol said they protected Gemma on Night 2, so nobody died, and on Day 2 the table voted out Opus, who showed citizen. Night 3 ended with Gemma's death, and on Day 3 Sol and Terra pushed hard on Sonnet, who was voted out and also showed killer. Both killers were out by Day 3, so the town won.
